## **2\. Product Background** {#2.-product-background}

Final-year students and fresh graduates often face a significant "experience gap" when transitioning from academia to the professional workforce. Despite having strong technical foundations, they frequently struggle with:

1. **Resume-JD Mismatch:** Inability to tailor their CVs to specific Job Descriptions.  
2. **Interview Anxiety:** Lack of exposure to high-pressure interview environments.  
3. **Feedback Void:** Not knowing why they were rejected or which specific knowledge areas to improve.  
4. **Limited Mentorship:** Difficulty in accessing real-world professionals for personalized guidance.  
5. **Professional Communication Gap:** Lack of professional email etiquette and formal communication skills, leading to negative first impressions and lost opportunities during initial HR contacts.

This project aims to bridge this gap by providing an end-to-end simulation of the hiring process, from CV screening to technical/behavioral interviews.

## **3\. Existing Systems** {#3.-existing-systems}

### **3.1 Aural \- AI Interview Platform**  {#3.1-aural---ai-interview-platform}

An AI-powered, open-source interview platform designed for both sides of the table. It helps candidates practice role-specific interviews and allows enterprises/managers to conduct structured, adaptive interviews at scale.

**Link:** [https://aural-ai.com/](https://aural-ai.com/)

**System actors:** Candidates (Students, Job Seekers) and Interviewers (Founders, Managers, HR).

**Features:**

* **Multi-mode Interfaces:** Supports text chat, natural voice conversations, and full video interviews.  
* **Adaptive AI Engine:** The AI adjusts follow-up questions, depth, and tone in real-time based on the candidate's answers.  
* **Comprehensive Assessments:** Supports open-ended questions, multiple-choice, rating scales, coding challenges, and whiteboard questions.  
* **Instant Analytics:** Automatically generates transcripts, session summaries, scores, and structured feedback for review.

**Pros:** 

* Highly flexible with multi-modal inputs (voice/text/video).  
* Provides adaptive conversations rather than static questions, simulating a real human interviewer.  
* Offers actionable, structured feedback to help candidates improve.  
* Open-source deployment options and REST API availability.

**Cons:**

1. As a newly launched platform (early 2026), its ecosystem for enterprise ATS (Applicant Tracking System) integration might not be as extensive as legacy systems.

### **3.2 HireVue** {#3.2-hirevue}

An enterprise-level, end-to-end hiring experience platform that utilizes video interviewing and AI-driven conversational assessments to evaluate candidates.

**Link:** [www.hirevue.com](https://www.hirevue.com)

**System actors:** Enterprises (HR/Recruiters, Hiring Managers), Candidates.

**Features:** 

* Asynchronous video interviews.  
* AI-backed candidate assessment and scoring.  
* ATS (Applicant Tracking System) integration.  
* Automated scheduling and text-based HR chatbots.

**Pros:** 

* Highly robust, scalable for large corporations, significantly speeds up the screening process for recruiters.

**Cons:** 

1.  Strictly a B2B product, not designed as a practice or learning platform for students.  
2. The AI evaluation can feel like a "black box" to candidates, offering them no actionable feedback to improve.  
3. Very expensive, making it inaccessible for individual users or educational institutions looking to train students.

## **4\. Business Opportunity** {#4.-business-opportunity}

Final-year Software Engineering students and recent graduates in Vietnam frequently encounter a significant gap between their academic preparation and the practical demands of real-world recruitment processes. Although they possess solid technical knowledge, most lack hands-on experience in navigating complete hiring pipelines and performing confidently under pressure during job interviews.

The key challenges include:

* Difficulty in aligning resumes with specific Job Descriptions and successfully passing Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS).  
* Limited exposure to end-to-end recruitment stages, from CV screening and technical assessments to multi-round interviews.  
* High levels of interview anxiety and insufficient confidence in one-on-one interactive situations.  
* Lack of detailed, constructive, and timely feedback to effectively identify and address personal weaknesses.  
* Very limited access to realistic practice environments and professional mentorship.  
* Professional Communication Gap: Lack of professional email etiquette and formal communication skills, leading to negative first impressions and lost opportunities during initial HR contacts.

While several interview preparation platforms currently exist — such as Interviewing.io, Pramp, FinalRoundAI, and various AI mock interview tools — most of them focus primarily on isolated practice questions, peer-to-peer sessions, or generic AI feedback. These tools treat each stage of recruitment as a separate, standalone activity, and none of them simulate the full, closed-loop recruitment pipeline as it operates in real enterprises. Critically, the market currently lacks a platform that integrates all sequential hiring stages — including CV filtering and ATS optimization, automated recruitment email communication, technical competency assessments, and multi-round AI-powered interviews — into a single, cohesive end-to-end experience.

This is the core problem InBlue is built to solve. Rather than offering fragmented preparation tools, InBlue simulates the entire interconnected recruitment chain, replicating how real hiring pipelines function from the first point of application through to final interview. By addressing this gap in pipeline-based simulation, the platform goes far beyond what existing solutions provide. It incorporates customizable multi-stage processes, immersive Virtual Interview Rooms, advanced RAG-based evaluation, behavior analysis, and a direct bridge connecting students with real companies.

With the rapid growth of Vietnam's technology sector and the increasing emphasis on practical skills and interview performance, the platform has strong market potential. InBlue not only helps students significantly improve their employability and confidence but also creates a valuable talent discovery channel for universities and enterprises. In the long term, InBlue can evolve into a comprehensive career preparation and recruitment ecosystem that benefits all stakeholders.

## **5\. Software Product Vision** {#5.-software-product-vision}

For Software Engineering students and fresh graduates who want to close the gap between academic learning and real-world job recruitment, InBlue is an intelligent AI-powered recruitment simulation platform that delivers a complete, realistic end-to-end hiring experience through an immersive Virtual AI Interview Room. 

InBlue enables students to practice with multiple simulated companies, progress through fully configurable recruitment pipelines, and receive detailed AI-driven evaluations using RAG technology. 

Unlike existing interview tools that offer only generic questions or limited feedback, InBlue recreates the entire recruitment journey — from resume screening, professional email communication simulation, assessment tests, to final virtual interviews — in a safe yet highly realistic environment. When complete, InBlue will significantly improve students' interview performance and employability while serving as a trusted bridge between talented graduates and technology companies in Vietnam and beyond.

## **6\. Project Scope & Limitations** {#6.-project-scope-&-limitations}

The scope of this project encompasses the design and implementation of a comprehensive AI-powered recruitment process simulation platform named InBlue. The system aims to provide Software Engineering students with a realistic, end-to-end hiring experience by combining currently implemented foundational features with significant new capabilities focused on enterprise simulation and full recruitment pipeline management.

Major features are categorized as follows:

### **6.1 Major Features \[\[\*BỔ SUNG THÊM\*\]\]**  {#6.1-major-features-[[*bổ-sung-thêm*]]}

FE-01: Public Landing and Marketing Hub – Attractive homepage showcasing the platform’s capabilities, interview modes, testimonials, and clear calls-to-action.

FE-02: Secure login using email/password and Google OAuth2, with role-based protected routing for USER, MENTOR, STAFF, and ADMIN.

FE-03: Multi-role Operational Dashboards – Dedicated and personalized management dashboards tailored for four distinct user roles: 

1. Candidate/Student Dashboard: Tracks active recruitment pipeline progress, upcoming interview schedules (Calendar), CV analysis match scores, and purchased JD packages.  
2. Mentor Dashboard: Displays assigned candidate interview sessions, upcoming 1-on-1 review schedules, candidate feedback ratings, and session histories.  
3. Staff/Reviewer Dashboard: Manages pending candidate submission evaluations, round grading queues, and manual review details.  
4. Admin Dashboard: Provides high-level platform analytics (user/mentor statistics, revenue logs, active pipeline metrics), along with management controls for kiosks, companies, and round templates.

FE-04: AI Interview Experience – End-to-end AI interview sessions driven by Python Microservices. Supports text and voice (STT/TTS) interactions, utilizing dynamic interview Blueprints and a real-time State Machine (Analyzer) for context-aware, follow-up conversational Q\&A.

FE-05: Mock Interviews with Mentors \- integration via Daily.co video calls, and post-session evaluation.

FE-06: Quiz Assessment – Question banks and dynamic quizzes.

FE-07: Community & Real-time Communication – Community feed, likes, comments, and real-time messaging via STOMP/WebSocket.

FE-08: Payment & Notification System – PayOS integration enables candidates to purchase participation packages for recruitment simulations based on specific job descriptions (JD Purchase), while also logging transaction history and automatically sending notifications.

FE-09: Configurable Recruitment Pipeline – Ability to create, orchestrate, and manage multi-stage sequential recruitment pipelines. Admin can customize up to 7 distinct rounds (CV Screening, Email Simulator, Quiz, Coding, Code Review, Mentor Interview, AI Interview).

FE-10: Advanced AI Evaluation & Feedback – Granular scoring and comprehensive performance reports powered by AnythingLLM (AI Router). Utilizes Multi-Workspace RAG for accurate, context-bound evaluation and tailored feedback, ensuring objective grading without LLM hallucination. (Đã bỏ hẳn chữ behavior analysis)

FE-11: Candidate Performance Analytics – Dashboards for tracking progress over time and comparing with benchmarks.

FE-12: AI-Powered CV Screening & Grading – A dedicated tool leveraging the AI Router for intelligent analysis. Candidates upload their CVs, and the system evaluates keyword alignment, experience relevance, and overall compatibility with a target Job Description. It produces a quantified match score and actionable improvement suggestions. An HR/Admin configuration interface enables authorized users to define scoring criteria and set minimum passing thresholds for the CV screening stage.

FE-13: Professional Email Simulator – A simulated email environment replicating real-world application correspondence. Candidates practice composing and responding to recruitment-related emails. The system routes the payload through the AI engine to automatically analyze grammar, tone, and professional structure, returning a detailed score and constructive feedback to help candidates refine their written communication skills.

FE-14: Coding Assessment – Supports algorithm and logic problem solving rounds with automated test case grading.

FE-15: Code Review Assessment – Supports code reading comprehension rounds where candidates detect and fix bugs. Submissions are automatically evaluated by the AI Router (AnythingLLM), matching candidate responses against established rubrics to grade their code-reading proficiency.

FE-16: Admin Round Template Management – Allows administrators to create, save, and reuse round templates for rapid recruitment pipeline setup.

FE-17: Physical Kiosk Booking & Holobox Display Integration – A scheduling manager allowing candidates to book timeslots at physical mock interview kiosks. Admin can manage kiosk locations and active status, while the system automatically calculates available slots with custom buffers between sessions. Additionally, it provides dedicated integration endpoints to fetch and project final evaluation reports (overall scores, skill radar charts, AI summary highlights) onto physical Holobox (3D holographic display) hardware stationed at the kiosk locations.

FE-18: Application Tracking and Round Workspace – Candidates can track submitted applications, view current round status, access the active assessment workspace, and review completed round feedback.

FE-19: Admin Content and Account Management – Admin can manage users, mentors, companies, job descriptions, posts, notifications, assessment repositories, coding problems, and code review problems.

FE-20: Staff Grading Workspace – Staff can review assigned candidate submissions, inspect AI-generated results, enter HR scores/notes, and approve or reject candidate progression.

FE-23: SWECom-adapted Competency Report – The system generates a standardized 0-100 competency report and radar chart based on selected SWECom technical skill areas and behavioral attributes.

### **6.2 Limitations & Exclusions** {#6.2-limitations-&-exclusions}

LI-01: Full integration with real enterprise HR systems and external ATS is not included; the system focuses on realistic simulation rather than direct connection with actual company recruitment platforms.

LI-02: Advanced computer vision features for detailed facial expression analysis, eye contact detection, and automated proctoring are not included in this phase.

LI-03: The platform primarily targets Software Engineering students; support for other majors or significantly different job domains is not planned in this version.

LI-04: Large-scale features such as virtual career fairs or mass recruitment events are excluded from the current scope.

LI-05: The platform supports English, Vietnamese, and Japanese UI localization, but complete professional translation review and full localization coverage for all generated AI content are outside the current scope.

LI-06: Real-time AI video avatar with lip synchronization and emotional intelligence is not planned; the current implementation relies on voice interaction with simple avatars.

## **2\. Management Approach** {#2.-management-approach}

The project will be managed using an Iterative Development approach combined with Git-flow. This allows flexibility for feedback and continuous adjustments while ensuring strict alignment with our core objectives. We will conduct daily stand-ups via Discord/Zalo to synchronize progress, and manage tasks systematically using GitHub Issues.

### **2.1 Project Process** {#2.1-project-process}

The team will apply an Iterative software development process model with Git-flow branching. The process includes:  
\- Task Management: Define tasks and track progress on GitHub Issues.  
\- Development: Write code on isolated feature branches.  
\- Pre-commit Checks: Automatically run Husky and ESLint to format code and catch errors before committing.  
\- Review & Merge: Submit Pull Requests (PRs) for peer review on GitHub before merging to the main branch.  
\- CI/CD: Automatically run tests and deployment builds via GitHub Actions upon merging.

### **2.2 Quality Management** {#2.2-quality-management}

To achieve quality objectives, the following approaches will be applied for both Frontend and Backend systems:

1. Defect Prevention: Peer code reviews via GitHub PRs. The Frontend team enforces strict standards using ESLint 9 and TypeScript Strict Mode. The Backend team ensures data integrity using spring-boot-starter-validation and SonarLint.  
2. Unit Testing: The Frontend UI components and logic are tested using Vitest. The Backend APIs (Spring Boot) are tested using JUnit 5 and Mockito, aiming for \>80% test coverage.  
3. Integration Testing: API endpoints and third-party integrations (e.g., PayOS, Cloudinary) are tested comprehensively using Swagger UI (springdoc-openapi) and Postman.  
4. System Testing (E2E): End-to-end testing is automated using Cypress to validate the entire user journey, from JWT authentication to AI interview submission on the web browser.

## **6\. Configuration Management** {#6.-configuration-management}

### **6.1 Document Management** {#6.1-document-management}

All project documents (Capstone Project Register, Report 1 – Project Introduction, Report 2 – Project Management Plan, SRS, Use Case Diagrams, System Architecture, ERD, User Manuals, Test cases, etc.) are centrally stored and version-controlled using **Google Drive** and **Google Docs**.

* **Organization**: Documents are categorized into clear folders corresponding to project phases (Initiation, Planning, Execution, Monitoring & Control, Closure).  
* **Change Tracking**: All modifications are recorded in the **Record of Changes** table at the beginning of each document. The Project Leader is responsible for final approval before submission to the Supervisor.  
* **Access Control**: Team members have edit rights, while the Supervisor has comment/view rights. This ensures transparency and effective collaboration.

### **6.2 Source Code Management** {#6.2-source-code-management}

The project source code is hosted on **GitHub** using **Git** as the version control system.

- **Branching Strategy**: The team follows the GitFlow workflow with main (production), develop (integration) and feature/\* branches for individual tasks.  
- **Workflow**: Each member develops on their own feature branch. Completed work is submitted via Pull Request for review before merging.  
- **Code Review**: All changes are reviewed by at least one other team member to maintain code quality and consistency.  
- **Commit Convention**: Descriptive commit messages are used to keep the project history clear and traceable.

# 

# **III. Software Requirement Specification** {#iii.-software-requirement-specification}

## **1\. Product Overview** {#1.-product-overview}

### **1.1 Product Overview \[\[\*CHỈNH SỬA\*\]\]**  {#1.1-product-overview-[[*chỉnh-sửa*]]}

**INBLUE** is an intelligent AI-powered recruitment simulation platform that delivers a complete, realistic end-to-end hiring experience. Designed primarily for Software Engineering students, the system bridges the "experience gap" by simulating enterprise hiring pipelines.

The platform recreates the entire recruitment journey—from AI-powered CV screening and ATS optimization, professional email communication simulation, technical assessments (Coding, Code Review, Quizzes), to multi-round virtual AI interviews using RAG technology. Additionally, it offers a real-world bridge by enabling Users to book 1:1 mock interviews with industry Mentors via embedded video calls.

The system is implemented as a distributed platform consisting of a Spring Boot backend, AI services developed with Python and FastAPI, a React-based web application, and a React Native mobile application. PostgreSQL is used for persistent data storage, while Redis manages temporary interview sessions and real-time state. The platform also integrates external services such as Gemini, AnythingLLM, Cloudinary, PayOS, Daily.co, and Docker Sandbox to support AI evaluation, file storage, payment, video interviews, and coding assessment.

![][image2]

### **1.2 Business Rules \[\[\*BỔ SUNG THÊM\*\]\]**  {#1.2-business-rules-[[*bổ-sung-thêm*]]}

* **Sequential Pipeline Rule:** Users must process sequentially through each configured round of a Job Description (JD). The system shall unlock the next round only after the current round is completed and verified.

* **Financial Integrity Rule:** All PayOS webhook events must pass checksum/signature verification before any payment status or JD entitlement is updated. If verification fails or the transaction is not successful, the system rejects the webhook event and does not mark the payment as completed, ensuring that no JD entitlement is granted for invalid or failed transactions.

* **Access Control Rule:** System access is strictly managed via JWT (JSON Web Token) Role-Based Access Control (Admin, Staff, Mentor, User).

* **Unique Email:** Email addresses in the users and mentor tables must be unique. Duplicate emails result in a 400 Bad Request error.         

* **OTP Expiry:** Password reset OTPs are stored in Redis with a strict 5-minute Time-To-Live (TTL). Expired OTPs are rejected. Successful resets immediately delete the OTP.

*  **GPA Normalization:** If the AI parser extracts a GPA on a 10-point scale (e.g., 8.0/10), the system automatically multiplies it by 0.4 to normalize it to a 4.0 scale.     

*  **Payment Flow:** Candidates must pay application fees directly via PayOS QR code. Applications remain PENDING until a successful webhook is received, advancing them to IN\_PROGRESS.         

* **Video Session Tracking:** Daily.co webhooks track join/leave events. A session is only marked COMPLETED when both parties (User and Mentor) have an endTime.         

* **AI Follow-up Logic:** If the AI determines a need to 'DRILL\_DOWN', it generates a follow-up question. Follow-up answers do not count directly towards the anchor question's average score.         

* **Auto-Advance Rounds:** When an ADMIN or STAFF scores a round and approves (isPass \= true), the system increments currentRoundOrder and creates a PENDING record for the next round.         

* **Community Post States:** Only posts with a PUBLISHED state are visible on the public news feed. DRAFT posts remain hidden.         

* **Soft-Delete JD Filter:** All Job Description queries implicitly filter isDeleted \= false to hide logically deleted jobs from candidates and admins.         

* **Mentor Selection State Flow:** The interview round status transitions sequentially from AWAITING\_MENTOR \-\> AWAITING\_CANDIDATE\_SELECT\_MENTOR \-\> PENDING (upon final mentor selection).         

* **Application Ownership Rule:** Users can only view and perform actions on their own applications. Access to another user's application or submission is denied.  
* **Submission State Rule:** A submission can only be created when the application is in the corresponding active round. Once a round is completed, additional submissions for that round are not allowed.  
* **Coding Sandbox Security Rule:** Candidate source code must be executed in an isolated Docker container with CPU, memory, execution-time, and network restrictions. Internet access is disabled during execution.  
* **AI Interview Timeout Rule:** When an AI interview session reaches its time limit, the system automatically terminates the session and saves its latest valid state and results.  
* **Payment Idempotency Rule:** Each PayOS webhook event must be processed only once. Repeated or duplicated webhook events must not create duplicate transactions or grant the same JD entitlement multiple times.

### **3.2 Authentication\[\[\*XEM LẠI\*\]\]**  {#3.2-authentication[[*xem-lại*]]}

#### ***3.2.1 User Register*** {#3.2.1-user-register}

**Function trigger:** User clicks 'Register' button on the landing page or login modal.

**Function description:** Enables new candidates to create a platform account using email credentials or Google Single Sign-On.

**Screen layout:** 

***![][image9]***

**Data:** Full Name, Email Address, Password, Confirm Password.

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** All fields are required; Email must follow standard email syntax format; Full Name minimum 2 characters; Password minimum 8 characters containing at least one uppercase letter, one digit, and one special character; Confirm Password must match Password.

  **• System Validation:** Email address must be unique in the system database.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Successful candidate registration creates a new user account with Candidate role, sets account status to pending verification, sends a 6-digit OTP verification code to the registered email, and redirects the candidate to the verification screen.

  **• Abnormal case:** Submitting an already registered email displays the error "Email address is already registered"; failing password complexity displays "Password does not meet complexity requirements"; mismatched password confirmation displays "Passwords do not match".

**Functionalities:** Registers new user entity, generates and sends welcome/OTP emails, and initiates account onboarding.

#### ***3.2.2 User Login*** {#3.2.2-user-login}

**Function trigger:** User accesses the login page or clicks 'Log In' in the navigation header.

**Function description:** Authenticates users of all system roles (Candidate, Mentor, Staff, Admin) using email credentials or Google Single Sign-On (SSO).

**Screen layout:** 

![][image10]

**Data:** Email/Username, Password, Authentication Token, User Profile (User ID, Email, Full Name, Role).

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** Email and Password fields are required; Email input must match standard email format.

  **• System Validation:** Credentials are verified against stored user account records.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Valid credentials establish an authenticated user session, store authentication tokens, initialize real-time notifications, and redirect the user to their role-specific landing page (Candidate to Candidate Home, Mentor to Mentor Portal, Staff to Staff Workspace, Admin to Admin Dashboard).

  **• Abnormal case:** Invalid credentials display the error message "Incorrect email or password". After 5 consecutive failed login attempts, the system temporarily locks the account for 15 minutes and dispatches an alert email. Deactivated accounts display the alert "Account locked by administrator".

**Functionalities:** Authenticates user credentials, supports "Remember Me" persistent session state, hydrates user role session, and initializes real-time communication channels upon login.

#### ***3.2.3 User Forgot & Reset Password*** {#3.2.3-user-forgot-&-reset-password}

**Function trigger:** User clicks 'Forgot Password?' link on the login page.

**Function description:** Provides a multi-step password recovery mechanism using email-based 6-digit One-Time Password (OTP) verification.

**Screen layout:** 

***![][image11]***

***![][image12]***

**Data:** Registered Email, 6-digit OTP Code, New Password, Confirm Password.

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** Email field is required; OTP code must be 6 numeric digits; New Password must satisfy password security policy.

  **• System Validation:** Email must exist in system database; OTP code must match active generated code.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Submitting a registered email dispatches a 6-digit OTP valid for 5 minutes. Entering the correct OTP unlocks the password reset form. Submitting a valid new password updates account credentials and invalidates all existing active sessions.

  **• Abnormal case:** Non-existent email displays "Email address not found"; invalid or expired OTP code displays "OTP code is invalid or expired"; 3 incorrect OTP entries lock the recovery session for 15 minutes.

**Functionalities:** Sends recovery OTP emails, verifies OTP codes, and updates user password credentials.

#### ***3.2.4 Account Settings & Password Change*** {#3.2.4-account-settings-&-password-change}

**Function trigger:** Authenticated user navigates to Settings tab in user profile or settings menu.

**Function description:** Allows users to manage system preferences (Dark/Light theme, language localizations) and change account password internally.

**Screen layout:** 

***![][image13]***

***![][image14]***

**Data:** Theme Mode Preference, Language Preference (English, Vietnamese, Japanese), Current Password, New Password.

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** All password fields are required; New Password must meet security policy and differ from Current Password.

  **• System Validation:** Current Password must be verified against current authenticated user credentials.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** User updates theme or language preferences with immediate UI response. Submitting valid password change updates account credentials while maintaining the active user session.

  **• Abnormal case:** Incorrect Current Password displays "Current password is incorrect"; New Password identical to Current Password displays "New password must differ from current password".

**Functionalities:** Updates system theme and language localization preferences, verifies and updates internal user passwords.

#### ***3.2.5 Candidate Profile*** {#3.2.5-candidate-profile}

**Function trigger:** Candidate accesses Candidate Account & Notifications page (\`/user/account\`).

**Function description:** Comprehensive profile management workspace displaying candidate bio, education history, work experience, technical/soft skills, social links, and PDF CV upload with automated AI JSON parsing.

**Screen layout:** 

***![][image15]***

**Data:** Candidate Profile (Phone, Address, LinkedIn URL, GitHub URL, Education Entries, Experience Entries, Project Entries, Technical Skills, Soft Skills, Attached CV File, Parsed CV Data).

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** CV upload restricted strictly to PDF format under 10MB size limit; LinkedIn and GitHub inputs must be valid URL formats; Phone number must follow valid phone syntax.

  **• System Validation:** Uploaded PDF file must contain readable text for AI extraction.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Uploading a PDF CV automatically triggers AI parsing to extract and populate candidate profile fields (skills, experience, education). Editing profile entries updates candidate records and recalculates profile completion percentage. Attached profile is automatically linked to job applications for ATS screening.

  **• Abnormal case:** Non-PDF file upload displays "File format must be PDF"; file exceeding 10MB displays "File size exceeds 10MB limit"; corrupted PDF displays "AI parsing failed: unreadable file text".

**Functionalities:** Manages candidate profile information, uploads and parses resume documents using AI services, calculates profile completion metrics.

#### ***3.2.6 Real-time Notification*** {#3.2.6-real-time-notification}

**Function trigger:** User clicks 'Notifications' bell icon in header or navigates to notifications page.

**Function description:** Centralized notification panel displaying real-time system alerts, application status updates, mentor session booking reminders, and feedback notifications.

**Screen layout:**  
**![][image16]![][image17]**

**Data:** Notification List (Notification ID, Recipient ID, Title, Message Text, Category Badge, Timestamp, Read Status).

**Validation:**

  **• System Validation:** User authorization required; Notifications scoped strictly to the authenticated recipient.

**Business rules:**

  **• Normal case:** System generates real-time push and inbox notifications upon key events (e.g., application status change, mentor session scheduled, STAR review submitted). User views notifications, clicks item to navigate to relevant workspace, and marks notifications as read or clears read items.

  **• Abnormal case:** Unauthenticated notification access is blocked; network disconnection displays offline cached alerts.

**Functionalities:** Dispatches real-time system notifications, tracks notification read statuses, routes users to event target pages, and provides notification list management.

#### ***3.3.1 Home, Features, Resources, Job Search & Company Showcase*** {#3.3.1-home,-features,-resources,-job-search-&-company-showcase}

**Function description:** Interactive job board and enterprise directory allowing candidates to search, filter, and view published IT Job Descriptions (JDs) and hiring company profiles.

**Screen layout:** 

# 

# ![][image18]![][image19]

![][image20]

***![][image21]![][image22]***

**Data:** Search Keyword, Level Filter, Salary Range, Job Description Details, Company Profile Information.

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** Search input sanitized against special character injection; Salary filter minimum must be non-negative and less than maximum limit.

  **• System Validation:** Only active and published job postings are returned.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Displays active Job Descriptions (JDs) with OPEN status. Applying keyword, level, or salary filters dynamically updates the job grid. Selecting a job opens job details; selecting a company opens the company showcase page.

  **• Abnormal case:** Search yielding no results displays "No job postings found matching your search criteria"; accessing closed or deleted postings displays "Job posting no longer active"; unauthenticated application attempts prompt login modal.

**Functionalities:** Searches and filters job descriptions, retrieves hiring company profile details, renders responsive job listings.

#### ***3.3.2 PayOS Application Checkout*** {#3.3.2-payos-application-checkout}

**Function trigger:** Candidate clicks 'Unlock Full JD Access' or 'Apply & Pay Fee' button on Job Description detail page.

**Function description:** Processes job application fees and job description access entitlement purchases via PayOS VietQR payment integration using a native single-screen payment modal.

**Screen layout:** 

![][image23]![][image24]![][image25]

**Data:** Payment Transaction Details (Checkout URL, VietQR Code Image, Bank Account Number, Bank Account Name, Payment Amount, Exact Transfer Reference Code, Transaction Status, Purchased JD Entitlement).

**Validation:**

  **• Input Validation:** Bank transfer reference code must match the generated transfer reference string exactly.

  **• System Validation:** Payment transaction window expires after 15 minutes; Transfer checksum and digital signature must be verified.

**Business rules:**

  **• Normal case:** Generating a payment request displays a native VietQR payment modal with a 15-minute countdown. Upon automated bank transfer verification, the transaction status updates to PAID. For JD Access purchases, full Job Description documentation, study materials, and application privileges are unlocked, and the purchase record is saved to the candidate's JD Purchase History tab. For application fee purchases, Round 1 (CV Screening) is automatically initialized.

  **• Abnormal case:** Transaction timeout (15 mins) cancels checkout; manual transaction cancellation marks the payment as failed or cancelled without granting any JD entitlement; reference code mismatch or bank verification failure causes the transaction to be rejected or flagged for system audit.

**Functionalities:** Generates VietQR payment requests, verifies background payment webhooks, unlocks full Job Description access rights, records purchase histories, and initializes application pipeline rounds upon payment verification.

#### ***3.3.3 Application History & Status Tracking*** {#3.3.3-application-history-&-status-tracking}

**Function trigger:** Candidate clicks 'Applications' tab in candidate dashboard.

**Function description:** Dashboard tracking all job applications submitted by the candidate, displaying progress status badges, active assessment round indicators, and evaluation score histories.

**Screen layout:** 

***![][image26]***

**Data:** Application List (Application ID, Job Title, Company Name, Applied Date, Current Round Order, Application Status, Round Details).

**Validation:** 

  **• System Validation:** Read-only data view restricted to candidate's own submitted applications.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Displays application history with real-time status badges (In Progress, Completed, Failed, Cancelled). Expanding an application shows the recruitment round pipeline stepper. Clicking active round workspace navigates to the current assessment round.

  **• Abnormal case:** Candidate attempting to view another user's application displays "Access denied"; clicking inactive or locked pipeline rounds displays "Complete current round to unlock next stage".

**Functionalities:** Tracks application progress, visualizes multi-stage recruitment pipeline steppers, routes candidate to active round workspace.

### **3.4 Assessment & Evaluation System\[\[\*XEM LẠI\*\]\]**  {#3.4-assessment-&-evaluation-system[[*xem-lại*]]}

#### ***3.4.1 Application CV Screening (File Upload & ATS Match)*** {#3.4.1-application-cv-screening-(file-upload-&-ats-match)}

**Function trigger:** Candidate enters Round 1 (CV Screening) in Application Workspace.

**Function description:** Allows candidate to submit CV PDF file for automated ATS match scoring against Job Description requirements.

**Screen layout:** 

# ![][image27]  ![][image28] 

**Data:** CV PDF Document, Application Round Details (Round ID, Compatibility Score, AI Analysis Feedback, Round Status).

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** File format restricted strictly to PDF under 10MB size limit.

  **• System Validation:** File content must contain valid extractable text.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Submitting a PDF CV triggers automated AI ATS analysis against job requirements. Score percentage \>= 60% passes the round and unlocks Round 2 advancement.

  **• Abnormal case:** Score \< 60% flags ATS rejection warning with improvement tips; empty or image-only PDF displays "Unable to extract CV text for ATS matching".

**Functionalities:** Processes CV PDF uploads, executes AI ATS match scoring algorithms, records assessment results in candidate application history.

#### ***3.4.2 Application Email Simulator*** {#3.4.2-application-email-simulator}

**Function trigger:** Candidate accesses Email Simulator round in Application Workspace.

**Function description:** Simulated enterprise inbox environment where candidate drafts professional response emails to business/HR scenario prompts, evaluated by AI for tone, grammar, and communication quality.

**Screen layout:** 

# ![][image29]![][image30] ![][image31]

**Data:** Subject Line, Email Body Content, Scenario Context, AI Evaluation Report (Tone Score, Clarity Score, Grammar Score, Overall Score, AI Notes).

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** Subject line required (min 5 characters); Email body content required (min 50 characters, max 3000 characters).

  **• System Validation:** Timed assessment round; Submission must be completed before time limit expires.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Candidate drafts and submits response email within time limit. Background AI evaluation grades communication tone, grammar, and structure. Start flags submission for Staff HR review.

  **• Abnormal case:** Submitting blank email is prevented by form validation; timer expiration auto-submits current draft; AI service failure queues submission for manual Staff grading.

**Functionalities:** Manages enterprise email simulation environment, evaluates writing responses using AI models, queues borderline submissions for HR review.

#### ***3.4.5 Application Coding Problem*** {#3.4.5-application-coding-problem}

**Function trigger:** Candidate starts Algorithmic Coding Problem round in Application Workspace.

**Screen layout: ![][image40]![][image41]![][image42]**

**![][image43]**

**Data:** Source Code String, Programming Language, Test Case Results (Execution Status, Time Elapsed, Memory Usage, Output Text).

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** Source code field cannot be blank; Programming language selection required.

  **• System Validation:** Execution time capped per test case (e.g., 2000ms limit); Memory consumption capped per execution.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Candidate writes code in Monaco IDE, tests against visible sample cases, and submits final solution. Code sandbox executes solution against 100% of hidden test cases. 100% test pass earns maximum score and unlocks next round.

  **• Abnormal case:** Code compilation error returns compiler output log; infinite loop or memory breach triggers Time Limit Exceeded (TLE) or Memory Limit Exceeded (MLE) error; failing hidden test case returns "Wrong Answer on test case X".

**Functionalities:** Embeds Monaco Code Editor, compiles and executes code inside isolated sandbox containers, validates code against visible and hidden test case suites.

  **• Abnormal case:** Booking an unavailable time slot displays "Slot no longer available"; mentor no-show flags session for Staff review refund or rescheduling.

**Functionalities:** Manages mentor booking and scheduling, integrates WebRTC 1-on-1 video call rooms, captures and displays structured STAR mentor feedback reports.

#### ***3.4.7 Application AI Interview & Physical Kiosk*** {#3.4.7-application-ai-interview-&-physical-kiosk}

**Function trigger:** Candidate launches an online AI Interview session in Application Workspace or checks in at a physical interview kiosk station using a 6-digit PIN code.

**Function description:** Real-time AI-powered interview engine supporting online web voice/text sessions, physical kiosk workstation sessions, FastAPI RAG question blueprints, dynamic follow-up drill-down questioning, STT voice input, TTS audio visualizer, 6-axis SWECOM competency report generation, and automated transmission of 3D performance reports to a Holobox holographic display device.

**Screen layout:**

# ![][image52]

# ![][image53] ![][image54]![][image55]

**Data:** Session Configuration (Mode, Difficulty, Language), Audio Stream / Transcript Text, Blueprint Questions, Kiosk Booking (Station ID, PIN Code, Scheduled Time Slot), 3D Holobox Payload (Candidate Name, Overall Score, Competency Metrics, Hologram Model Details), Session Results.

**Validation:** 

  **• Input Validation:** Microphone permission required for voice mode; Kiosk 6-digit PIN code must match active booking slot.

  **• System Validation:** Kiosk check-in allowed within 10-minute window of booked time slot; Real-time WebSocket connection active during session.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Online or walk-in kiosk candidates complete the AI interview. The AI engine dynamically generates follow-up questions. Upon session completion, the automated AI evaluation pipeline generates the 6-axis SWECOM competency chart and hiring recommendation, and automatically transmits 3D evaluation data to the Holobox holographic display device.                  

  **• Abnormal case:** Microphone permission denial triggers automatic fallback to text chat mode; WebSocket disconnections auto-pause the session state in Redis, allowing the candidate to resume the interview seamlessly; an invalid PIN displays "PIN code incorrect or expired"; check-in attempts outside the 10-minute window display "Station check-in window closed"; Holobox hardware disconnections queue offline transmission for later processing.                  

**Functionalities:** Conducts AI avatar interview sessions, transcribes voice audio via Speech-to-Text, synthesizes AI speech via Text-to-Speech, calculates 6-axis SWECOM competency matrix, handles physical kiosk PIN check-in verification, and transmits 3D assessment reports to Holobox holographic displays.

**Validation:** 

  **• System Validation:** Report generation requires completed assessment rounds; Access restricted to the application candidate or authorized HR staff.

**Business rules:** 

  **• Normal case:** Upon completing recruitment pipeline rounds, the system automatically compiles evaluation metrics and renders the Candidate Competency Report (\`UC-110\`). The candidate views their overall score, technical vs. human indices, 6-axis competency radar chart, detailed AI narrative summary, and personalized recommended next steps for career growth.

  **• Abnormal case:** Attempting to view report for an incomplete application displays "Assessment report available upon round completion"; unauthorized access displays "Access denied".

**Functionalities:** Aggregates multi-round evaluation metrics, renders 6-axis competency radar charts, calculates technical and behavioral indices, generates qualitative AI summary narratives, and provides targeted skill development recommendations.

## **4\. Non-Functional Requirements** {#4.-non-functional-requirements}

### **4.1 External Interfaces\[\[\*XEM LẠI\*\]\]**  {#4.1-external-interfaces[[*xem-lại*]]}

**The system interacts securely with external components:** PayOS for webhook-based payment processing, Daily.co for WebRTC 1-on-1 video interviews, a distributed AI system comprising AnythingLLM (acting as an AI Router/Gateway) and Python AI Microservices (integrating the Gemini API) for submission evaluation, blueprint generation, and real-time interview orchestration, Cloudinary for cloud-based asset and document storage, an Email System for automated notification and OTP delivery, and the Holobox 3D Display Interface for candidate evaluation 3D holographic rendering.

###### *Table 17 \- External Interfaces*

| Interface | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Payment Gateway API | Online payment processing via PayOS webhooks; handles transaction creation requests, status verification, and returns checkout URLs and payment status updates. |
| Email Service | Send notifications, system alerts, and one-time passwords (OTP) to users and candidates. |
| AI Subsystems (AnythingLLM & Python Microservices) | The AI system is divided into two main pillars:  \- AnythingLLM (AI Router / Gateway): Acts as a central router managing Multi-Workspaces and flexibly rotating API Keys/Models. It orchestrates tasks such as CV parsing/scoring, Email evaluation, Code Review, and test generation, while leveraging RAG to strictly confine the context.  \- Python Microservices: Integrates LLMs (Gemini) to process the AI Interview pipeline: generating structured interview plans (Blueprints), analyzing context, and making real-time interactive Q\&A decisions (Analyzer & State Machine). |
| Video Service | Handles WebRTC 1-on-1 video interviews via Daily.co API; processes room creation requests and provides unique video room URLs for interview sessions. |
| Cloud Storage | Cloud-based media and document storage via Cloudinary; handles image and PDF CV file uploads and provides secure file URLs. |
| Holobox 3D Display Interface | API endpoint providing structured candidate evaluation DTOs (scores, radar metrics, AI summary) for 3D holographic rendering on Holobox hardware. |

### 

### **4.2 Quality Attributes** {#4.2-quality-attributes}

***4.2.1 Usability***

Cross-Browser Compatibility: The Daily.co WebRTC video interview interface is designed to support recent versions of Chrome, Safari, and Edge.  
Responsive Interfaces: Customized dashboards for USER, MENTOR, STAFF, and ADMIN, optimized for the main supported screen sizes.

***4.2.2 Reliability***

Session Reliability: Redis stores temporary AI interview session state with a time-to-live (TTL). Expired sessions are handled gracefully to avoid stale or hanging sessions.  
AI Resiliency: Limited retry and fallback handling are used where possible so temporary AI service errors can be reported without crashing the application.

***4.2.3 Performance***

API Response Time: Under normal demo or staging load, common APIs should normally respond within approximately 1–3 seconds. AI-related requests may take longer and use a limited retry mechanism of up to 3 attempts.  
Real-time Updates: Community chat and feed interactions utilize WebSockets for near real-time data delivery, depending on network and server conditions.

***4.2.4 Security***

Authentication & Authorization: Uses JWT (JSON Web Token) for API security. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) enforces strict privileges for USER, MENTOR, STAFF, and ADMIN.  
OAuth2 Integration: Supports secure single sign-on (SSO) via Google OAuth2.  
Webhook Security: Incoming PayOS webhooks must be verified using digital checksums to prevent payment fraud.

* HTTPS encryption when deployed to staging or production environments  
* JWT authentication  
* Password hashing

## **5\. Requirement Appendix** {#5.-requirement-appendix}

### **5.1 Business Rules\[\[\*XEM LẠI\*\]\]**  {#5.1-business-rules[[*xem-lại*]]}

###### *Table 18 \- Business Rules*

| ID | Rule Definition |
| :---: | ----- |
| BR-01 | Unique Email: Email addresses in the \`users\` and \`mentor\` tables must be unique. Duplicate emails result in a 400 Bad Request error. |
| BR-02 | OTP Expiry: Password reset OTPs are stored in Redis with a strict 5-minute Time-To-Live (TTL). Expired OTPs are rejected. Successful resets immediately delete the OTP. |
| BR-03 | GPA Normalization: If the AI parser extracts a GPA on a 10-point scale (e.g., 8.0/10), the system automatically multiplies it by 0.4 to normalize it to a 4.0 scale. |
| BR-04 | Payment Flow: Candidates purchase access to a Job Description (JD) through PayOS QR payment. When a successful PayOS webhook is verified, the system records the payment as completed and creates a PURCHASED JD entitlement for the candidate. The candidate can then use this entitlement to apply for the JD, at which point a new Application is created with IN\_PROGRESS status and the first configured recruitment round is initialized. Repeated valid webhooks for the same transaction must not create duplicate entitlements. |
| BR-05 | Video Session Tracking: Daily.co webhooks track join/leave events. A session is only marked COMPLETED when both parties (User and Mentor) have an endTime. |
| BR-06 | AI Blueprint TTL: AI interview blueprints are stored in Redis. If the user does not start the interview before the Redis TTL expires, the PostgreSQL session state changes to CANCELLED. |
| BR-07 | AI Follow-up Logic: If the AI determines a need to 'DRILL\_DOWN', it generates a follow-up question. Follow-up answers do not count directly towards the anchor question's average score. |
| BR-08 | Auto-Advance Rounds: When an ADMIN scores a round and approves (isPass \= true), the system increments \`currentRoundOrder\` and creates a PENDING record for the next round. |
| BR-09 | Community Post States: Only posts with a PUBLISHED state are visible on the public news feed. DRAFT posts remain hidden. |
| BR-10 | Soft-Delete JD Filter: All Job Description queries implicitly filter \`isDeleted \= false\` to hide logically deleted jobs from candidates and admins. |
| BR-11 | Mentor Selection State Flow: The interview round status transitions sequentially from AWAITING\_MENTOR \-\> AWAITING\_CANDIDATE\_SELECT\_MENTOR \-\> PENDING (upon final mentor selection). |
| BR-12 | Sequential Pipeline Rule: Users must process sequentially through each configured round of a Job Description (JD). The system shall unlock the next round only after the current round is completed and verified. |
| BR-13 | Financial Integrity Rule: PayOS webhooks must pass checksum/signature verification before payment completion. Invalid or failed transactions are rejected or marked as failed, and no JD entitlement is granted. |
| BR-14 | Access Control Rule: System access is strictly managed via JWT (JSON Web Token) Role-Based Access Control (Admin, Staff, Mentor, User). |
| BR-15 | Assessment Passing Rule: Each assessment round uses its configured passing threshold. A candidate can proceed to the next round only when the current round is passed or manually approved by Staff. |
| BR-16 | Kiosk Booking Rule: A kiosk session can only be entered using a valid booking/PIN within the allowed check-in window. Expired or invalid PINs must be rejected. |
| BR-18 | Content Moderation Rule: Community posts, reviews, and feedback may be hidden, rejected, or removed by Staff/Admin if they violate platform policy. |
|  BR-19 | Notification Rule: System notifications must be linked to a target user and maintain read/unread status until the user marks them as read. |
|  BR-20 | Application Ownership Rule: Candidates can only view and act on their own applications, while Staff/Admin can access applications assigned to their operational role. |
|  BR-21 | Role Scope Rule: The system supports four authenticated roles: USER, MENTOR, STAFF, and ADMIN. There is no separate HR/company role in the current scope. Company-side HR participation is simulated internally by platform Staff/Admin. |
| BR-22 | Internal Simulation Rule: INBLUE is an internal recruitment simulation platform for students to practice interview pipelines. External companies may provide reference job content with permission, but company representatives do not directly operate inside the system. |
| BR-23 | Company Display Permission Rule: Company information, logos, and job descriptions may be displayed only when the team has permission or uses approved simulated/reference content. |
| BR-24 | Job Type Scope Rule: The platform focuses on full-time recruitment simulation.  |
| BR-25 | JD Configuration Rule: Job Descriptions, recruitment rounds, and assessment templates are configured by Admin/Staff, not by external company HR users. Company-provided content can be used only as reference input. |
| BR-26 | JD Template Rule: Admin should use reusable JD and round templates for common full-time recruitment pipelines to avoid configuring every JD from scratch. |
| BR-27 | Experience Continuation Rule: Because the system is designed for learning and simulation, a failed round may still allow the candidate to continue the experience if the configured simulation mode permits it. The result remains recorded as failed for feedback/reporting. |
| BR-28 | Professional Review Rule: Pass/fail decisions for professional or manually reviewed rounds are made by assigned Staff reviewers within the simulated internal process, not by external company HR. |
| BR-29 | Mentor Compensation Scope Rule: Mentor compensation is handled as an external company/accounting process and is outside the current system scope. The platform records mentor sessions and feedback, but does not calculate salary or revenue sharing. |
| BR-30 | Video Recording Scope Rule: Video recording storage is handled through Daily.co/external service capability when enabled. INBLUE does not guarantee local video backup storage inside the application. Admin may coordinate external access if recordings are required. |
| BR-31 | Kiosk Scheduling Rule: Admin configures kiosk stations and available interview slots in advance. Candidates can only book from available slots exposed by the system. |
| BR-32 | Chat Scope Rule: Real-time chat supports plain text messages only. Image, file, and media attachments are outside the current chat scope. |
| BR-33 | Deployment Scope Rule: Self-hosting hardware reliability, physical power backup, and production infrastructure operations are non-functional deployment concerns and are outside the core functional scope unless explicitly included in deployment documentation. |
| BR-34 | Application Round Lock Rule: Candidates can only access the current active round of an application. Previous completed rounds are read-only, and future rounds remain locked until the pipeline rule unlocks them. |
| BR-35 | Score Threshold Configuration Rule: Assessment pass thresholds must be configurable per round or template. The system must use the active configured threshold when calculating pass/fail status. |
| BR-36 | Manual Override Rule: Staff may manually override or confirm automated assessment outcomes when the workflow requires human review. Manual decisions must be stored with reviewer notes. |
| BR-37 | Audit Trail Rule: Important operational actions such as payment confirmation, grading, mentor assignment, content moderation, and account status changes should be traceable through stored records or logs. |
| BR-38 | SWECom Adaptation Rule: Competency radar reports must be based on selected SWECom technical skill areas and behavioral attributes that are relevant to the simulated recruitment process. The system does not claim to assess every SWECom skill area. |
| BR-39 | Competency Score Normalization Rule: Scores from different assessment rounds must be normalized to a 0-100 scale before being aggregated into the competency chart. Scores outside the valid range must be clamped to the nearest valid boundary. |
| BR-40 | Competency Level Mapping Rule: Overall competency levels must be derived from normalized scores using the configured level thresholds, mapped to SWECom-inspired levels such as Technician, Entry Level Practitioner, Practitioner, Technical Leader, and Senior Software Engineer. |
| BR-41 | Competency Report Availability Rule: The competency radar report is available only after sufficient assessment data has been completed and stored.  |
| BR-42 | Competency Interpretation Rule: The radar chart is used as a learning and feedback visualization for simulation purposes. It must not be presented as an official hiring certification or a complete professional SWECom assessment. |
| BR-43 | Standardized Scoring Scale Rule: All assessment scores displayed or aggregated by the system must use a standardized 0-100 scale. |
| BR-17 | Submission Rule: Candidates can submit only the current active round. After a round is completed, the candidate cannot submit that round again. |
| BR-44 | Coding Sandbox Rule: Candidate code must be executed through a separate sandbox service with a configured execution time limit. |
| BR-45 | AI Interview Timeout Rule: When the configured interview time expires, the system automatically ends the interview session, submits the current attempt, saves the final state, and prevents further answers. |

### **5.2 Common Requirements\[\[\*XEM LẠI\*\]\]**  {#5.2-common-requirements[[*xem-lại*]]}

* User Authentication and Security: Implement stateless authentication using JSON Web Tokens (JJWT), Spring Security OAuth2, and Google OAuth2 integration. Enforce strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) across 5 primary roles (USER, MENTOR, STAFF, ADMIN,GUEST).  
* Multilingual Support: Ensure the Web and Mobile interfaces fully support English, Vietnamese, and Japanese through comprehensive i18n localization structures.  
* Data Management and Storage: Securely manage relational data and AI RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) vector embeddings using PostgreSQL (pgvector), alongside Redis for high-speed state caching.  
* File and Media Handling: Support scalable and secure multimedia storage utilizing Cloudinary for CV parsing, user avatars, and candidate attachments, with strict upload limits configured via Tomcat.  
* Performance and Real-time Processing: Provide real-time communication via Spring Boot WebSockets for instant in-app notifications and live chat functionalities, alongside background cron scheduling for data synchronization (e.g., automated expiration of Job Descriptions).  
* Third-Party Integrations: Facilitate secure payment processing via the PayOS gateway and establish reliable WebRTC video calling rooms via Daily.co for 1-1 mentoring and interview sessions.  
* Accessibility and Cross-Platform: Deliver a seamless and consistent user experience across Web (React) and Mobile (React Native) applications, with specialized workflows for offline Kiosk bookings and offline Mentor sessions.

###### *Table 22 \- Table Descriptions*

| No | Table | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | User | Stores account information for all system actors including candidates, HR staff, and admins.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: none |
| 2 | Mentor | Represents expert evaluators who conduct 1-on-1 mentor review sessions.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: none |
| 3 | CandidateProfile | Stores comprehensive profile details like education, skills, work experience, and CV data.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: user\_id → User.id, application\_id → Application.id |
| 4 | Application | Represents a candidate's overall application for a specific Job Description.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: user\_id → User.id, jd\_id → JobDescription.id |
| 5 | ApplicationDetail | Tracks a candidate's progression and scores through individual interview/recruitment rounds.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: application\_id → Application.id, round\_id → Round.id, mentor\_review\_id → MentorReview.id, mentor\_id → Mentor.id, session\_id → Session.id, ai\_interview\_session\_id → InterviewSession.id |
| 6 | JobDescription | Stores job requirements used as context for AI evaluation, candidate matching, and round pipelines.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: company\_id → Company.id |
| 7 | Round | Defines specific recruitment rounds (e.g., CV screening, quiz, coding, AI interview, mentor review).\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: jd\_id → JobDescription.id, reviewer\_id → User.id |
| 8 | Company | Represents the organization offering job openings.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: none |
| 9 | InterviewSession | Manages context, settings, transcript history, and evaluation scores for AI mock interview sessions.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: user\_id → User.id, application\_detail\_id → ApplicationDetail.id |
| 10 | MentorReview | Stores detailed STAR model feedback and evaluation scores provided by mentors.\- Primary keys: id (maps to session\_id)\- Foreign keys: session\_id → Session.id, mentor\_id → Mentor.id, user\_id → User.id |
| 11 | Session | Manages active connection state and metadata for live video/audio 1-on-1 sessions (Daily.co / Kiosk).\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: user\_id → User.id, mentor\_id → Mentor.id, kiosk\_id → Kiosk.id |
| 12 | MentorFeedback | Stores qualitative feedback and ratings given by candidates regarding a mentor's session performance.\- Primary keys: id (maps to session\_id)\- Foreign keys: session\_id → Session.id, mentor\_id → Mentor.id, user\_id → User.id |
| 13 | Payment | Tracks financial transactions, such as wallet top-ups or JD package purchases via PayOS.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: user\_id → User.id, jd\_id → JobDescription.id |
| 14 | Notification | Stores system-generated alerts and notifications for users.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: user\_id → User.id |
| 15 | Post | Represents discussion or community posts created by users.\- Primary keys: post\_id\- Foreign keys: author\_id → User.id |
| 16 | PostLike | Tracks user likes on community posts.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: post\_id → Post.post\_id, user\_id → User.id |
| 17 | PostComment | Tracks comments added to community posts.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: post\_id → Post.post\_id, user\_id → User.id, parent\_comment\_id → PostComment.id |
| 18 | QuestionBank | Central repository for quiz, coding, and interview questions.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: question\_category\_id → QuestionCategory.id |
| 19 | QuestionCategory | Categorizes questions within the question bank by topics or domains.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: none |
| 20 | TemplateRound | Defines the configuration and structure of a specific interview round within a pipeline template.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: template\_id → InterviewTemplate.id |
| 21 | InterviewTemplate | Manages overarching predefined templates for entire recruitment pipelines.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: none |
| 22 | ChatMessage | Stores real-time chat messages exchanged between candidates and mentors.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: sender\_id → User.id / Mentor.id, recipient\_id → User.id / Mentor.id |
| 23 | LlmChatLog | Logs comprehensive telemetry data and payload history for all API requests executed via the AI microservice, including trace ID, session ID, target workspace (e.g., CV\_SCREENING, CODE\_REVIEW, AI\_INTERVIEW), user prompt payload, AI response text, prompt/completion token metrics, and API response duration.                |
| 24 | CodeReviewProblem | Stores code snippets and review challenges for technical code review assessments.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: none |
| 25 | CodingProblem | Stores algorithmic challenges and test cases for the coding round.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: none |
| 26 | EmailInbox | Tracks emails and submissions sent to or received by the automated email evaluation service.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: application\_id → Application.id |
| 27 | JdPurchase | Stores purchase records and unlock quotas for Job Descriptions via PayOS.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: user\_id → User.id, jd\_id → JobDescription.id, payment\_id → Payment.id |
| 28 | Kiosk | Manages physical Inblue AI interview kiosk hardware devices and locations.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: none |
| 29 | KioskBooking | Manages candidate interview session bookings at physical kiosks using a 6-digit PIN.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: kiosk\_id → Kiosk.id, applicant\_user\_id → User.id, application\_detail\_id → ApplicationDetail.id |
| 30 | KioskSchedule | Defines operating schedules, available days, and slot durations for physical interview kiosks.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: kiosk\_id → Kiosk.id |
| 31 | JourneySummary | Aggregates candidate interview journey summaries and 6-axis SWECOM competency radar evaluation results.\- Primary keys: id\- Foreign keys: application\_id → Application.id |
| 32 | MentorInterviewBooking | Tracks candidate 1-on-1 mentor interview session reservations, WebRTC room URLs, session fees, and booking status. \- Primary keys: id \- Foreign keys: applicant\_user\_id → User.id, mentor\_user\_id → User.id, application\_detail\_id → ApplicationDetail.id |

# **V. Software Testing Documentation** {#v.-software-testing-documentation}

## **1\. Scope of Testing** {#1.-scope-of-testing}

*The scope of testing covers both backend services and end-to-end user flows of the INBLUE AI-Powered Recruitment & Mentoring System. Functional areas in scope include authentication, AI Interviews (text/voice), 1-1 interview , job application flows, code and quiz assessment, community interaction, and financial operations via PayOS.​*

*Testing is performed on a dedicated test environment including application servers, PostgreSQL database, Redis, and React web clients using Google Chrome on Windows 10/11. Constraints include using a staging environment with test payment gateways (PayOS sandbox) and some assumptions on third-party service availability (FastAPI AI grading, Daily.co SDK).*

## **2\. Test Strategy** {#2.-test-strategy}

### **2.1 Testing Types** {#2.1-testing-types}

*The project applies functional testing to verify business requirements for all core features such as authentication, onboarding, AI mock interviews, live mentoring video calls, job application workflows, and financial flows. Input validation and boundary testing are used extensively for fields like email, password complexity, prices, dates, scores, ratings, and bank account information to ensure robustness against invalid and edge-case inputs.​*

*Security and access control testing is performed at a basic level, covering token expiry and refresh, logout behavior, role-based access for Candidate/Mentor/Admin/Staff, and restrictions during refund processing. Usability and UI testing is executed for responsive web views, checking layout, responsiveness, scroll behavior, keyboard overlay, and visibility of critical buttons on various screen sizes.​*

*Integration and workflow testing validates end-to-end business scenarios such as job application payments via PayOS, Daily.co video integration, AI-based CV screening and AI Interview grading, and administrative dashboards. Basic performance and reliability checks are included, such as concurrent submission handling, network disconnection during recording or payment, and graceful error handling without data loss.*

### **2.2 Test Levels \[\[\*XEM LẠI\*\]\]**  {#2.2-test-levels-[[*xem-lại*]]}

*The following test levels are applied in this project:*

*Unit Testing: Executed comprehensively on both backend services and frontend components. A total of 108 unit test cases across 36 functions were designed and executed using JUnit 5, Mockito (Backend), and Vitest (Frontend), validating Normal, Abnormal, and Boundary conditions.*

*Integration/System Testing: Performed on functional features such as Authentication, Job Payment, Assessment, AI Interview, Mentor, Community, Staff Operations, System Administration, with 81 system test cases executed.​*

*Acceptance Testing: Internal acceptance is considered achieved after the second test iteration, where all test cases across features reached 100% pass rate and 100% successful coverage.*

###### *Table 23 \- Test Levels*

| Type of Tests | Test Level |  |  |  |
| ----- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
|  | **Unit** | **Integration** | **System** | **Acceptance** |
| Functional & validation tests | X | X | X | X |
| Security & access control |  | X | X | X |
| Usability & UI checks |  |  | X | X |
| Performance & reliability |  | X | X | X |

## **2\. Installation Guides** {#2.-installation-guides}

### **2.1 System Requirements** {#2.1-system-requirements}

To ensure stable system operation, the following tools must be installed on your local machine:

• **Node.js** (v18 or higher) and **pnpm** (Package Manager for Frontend).

• **Java Development Kit (JDK) 21 and Maven 3.9+ (or the included Maven Wrapper).** 

• **Python 3.10 or higher. Python 3.11 is used by the LLM and compiler Docker images.**

• **PostgreSQL 15+ with JSONB support. Docker Engine is additionally required for the isolated coding sandbox.**

• **Redis Server for caching and interview session state management.**

### **2.2 Installation Instruction** {#2.2-installation-instruction}

#### **2.2.1 Backend Core Setup (Java Spring Boot)** {#2.2.1-backend-core-setup-(java-spring-boot)}

##### ***2.2.1.1 Clone the Backend Repository*** {#2.2.1.1-clone-the-backend-repository}

git clone https://github.com/Kdz198/Inblue.git

cd Inblue

##### ***2.2.1.2 Configure Environment Variables (application.properties)*** {#2.2.1.2-configure-environment-variables-(application.properties)}

Open \`src/main/resources/application.properties\` and ensure the following essential variables are configured:

• Database: \`SPRING\_DATASOURCE\_URL\`, \`SPRING\_DATASOURCE\_USERNAME\`, \`SPRING\_DATASOURCE\_PASSWORD\`, \`SPRING\_JPA\_HIBERNATE\_DDL\_AUTO\`, \`SHOW\_SQL\`

• **Cloudinary:** \`CLOUDINARY\_CLOUD\_NAME\`, \`CLOUDINARY\_API\_KEY\`, \`CLOUDINARY\_API\_SECRET\`

• Daily.co: \`DAILY\_API\_URL\`, \`DAILY\_DOMAIN\`, \`DAILY\_API\_KEY\`, \`DAILY\_WEBHOOK\_URL\`, and \`MENTOR\_CHARGE\_AMOUNT\`

• **Redis:** \`REDIS\_HOST\`, \`REDIS\_PORT\`, \`REDIS\_USERNAME\`, \`REDIS\_PASSWORD\`

• PayOS: \`PAYOS\_CLIENT\_ID\`, \`PAYOS\_API\_KEY\`, \`PAYOS\_CHECKSUM\_KEY\`, \`PAYOS\_CANCEL\_URL\`, and \`PAYOS\_RETURN\_URL\`; AI integrations: \`PYTHON\_LLM\_URL\`, \`ANYTHING\_LLM\_URL\`, \`ANYTHING\_LLM\_API\_KEY\`, and \`COMPILER\_SERVICE\_URL\`.

• Security: \`JWT\_SECRET\` and \`JWT\_EXPIRATION\_MS\`. • Google OAuth: \`GOOGLE\_CLIENT\_ID\`, \`GOOGLE\_CLIENT\_SECRET\`, \`GOOGLE\_REDIRECT\_URI\`, and \`GOOGLE\_SCOPE\`. • Frontend and API documentation: \`FE\_URL\`, \`APP\_OPENAPI\_PROD\_URL\`, and \`APP\_OPENAPI\_DEV\_URL\`. • SMTP mail: \`SPRING\_MAIL\_HOST\`, \`SPRING\_MAIL\_PORT\`, \`SPRING\_MAIL\_USERNAME\`, and \`SPRING\_MAIL\_PASSWORD\`

##### ***2.2.1.3 How to retrieve each important configuration*** {#2.2.1.3-how-to-retrieve-each-important-configuration}

**a. PostgreSQL Database Connection String**

• **Format:** \`jdbc:postgresql://\<HOST\>:5432/\<DB\_NAME\>\`

• Example: \`jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/inblue\_db\`

**b. JWT Secret Key**

• Generate your own Base64 string or long random string.

• Example using OpenSSL: \`openssl rand \-base64 32\`

**c. Email (SMTP Gmail)**

• Use a standard Gmail account.

• Open your Google Account Settings \-\> Security \-\> Turn on **2-Step Verification**.

• Create an **App Password**.

• Paste the App Password into \`SPRING\_MAIL\_PASSWORD\`.

**d. Cloudinary**

• Access: https://cloudinary.com

• Create a free account and go to your **Dashboard**.

• Copy the following fields: \`Cloud Name\`, \`API Key\`, \`API Secret\`.

**e. Google Login (OAuth)**

• Access: https://console.cloud.google.com

• Navigate to **APIs & Services \-\> Credentials**.

• Click **Create Credentials** \-\> **OAuth Client ID**.

• Retrieve the \`Client ID\` and \`Client Secret\`.

**f. Daily.co (Video Call SDK)**

• Access: https://daily.co

• Create an account and navigate to the **Developers** dashboard.

• Generate a master \`API Key\` and retrieve your Daily domain.

**g. Redis**

• You can use Redis Cloud or Self-host via Docker.

• Copy your \`Host\`, \`Port\`, and \`Password\`.

• Default local port is \`6379\`.

**h. PayOS (Payment Gateway)**

• Register a PayOS Merchant account at https://payos.vn.

• Create a new payment channel.

• Go to the payment channel settings to retrieve: \`Client ID\`, \`API Key\`, and \`Checksum Key\`.

##### ***2.2.1.4 Database Schema Initialization*** {#2.2.1.4-database-schema-initialization}

The Backend API currently uses Hibernate schema auto-generation for local development. This is schema initialization rather than a versioned database migration.

• For local development, set \`spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update\`. For production, use a controlled migration strategy instead of relying on automatic schema updates.

• Upon the first application startup, all required tables will be automatically created in your PostgreSQL database.

##### ***2.2.1.5 Run API*** {#2.2.1.5-run-api}

• Resolve dependencies and build:

  mvn clean install \-DskipTests

• Start the Spring Boot Application:

  mvn spring-boot:run

• **Swagger Documentation:** Access \`http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui/index.html\` after the server starts.

Set \`VITE\_API\_BASE\_URL\` to point to the running Backend API. Ensure Backend Step 5 is completed and the API is running before attempting to log in on the Web App.

##### ***2.2.3.1 Navigate to AI Directory*** {#2.2.3.1-navigate-to-ai-directory}

Clone the Python AI services repository. It contains separate services for LLM processing and code execution.

git clone https://github.com/Kdz198/Inblue-LLM-Service.git; cd Inblue-LLM-Service

***2.2.3.4 Run the API. Start the LLM service from the \`LLMService\` directory with: uvicorn main:app \--reload \--port 8000\. The Docker sandbox runs separately in its own container.***
