### **2.3 Architecture & Networking Overview** {#2.3-architecture-&-networking-overview}

The INBLUE Platform operates as a distributed multi-service architecture consisting of a modular Spring Boot backend, a Python LLM service, a Docker-based compiler service, a React web application, and a React Native kiosk application. To ensure security and performance, especially in a Homelab or production environment, the networking is structured as follows:

• **Zero-Trust Network (Cloudflare Tunnels):** Direct internet exposure of ports is strictly prohibited. Instead, \`cloudflared\` is used to create outbound tunnels from the server to Cloudflare's edge. All incoming traffic (HTTP/HTTPS) is routed through this secure tunnel.

• **API Gateway / Reverse Proxy:** The Java Spring Boot backend acts as the primary business API and integration layer, handling authentication, application workflow, and communication with external services. It internally communicates with the FastAPI AI service via internal Docker networking.

• **Internal Only Services:** Critical components such as PostgreSQL (Port 5432\) and Redis (Port 6379\) are strictly bound to the internal Docker network (\`bridge\`) or \`localhost\`. They are not exposed to the public internet, preventing brute-force attacks.

### **2.4 Docker Deployment (Homelab / Production Setup)** {#2.4-docker-deployment-(homelab-/-production-setup)}

For production deployment, INBLUE uses Docker images managed through Dockge. The Backend, LLM service, compiler service, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Cloudflare Tunnel are deployed as separate components.

#### **2.4.1 Install Docker Engine & Docker Compose** {#2.4.1-install-docker-engine-&-docker-compose}

To prepare the host machine (Ubuntu Server LTS), execute the following commands to install Docker Engine:

sudo apt-get update

sudo apt-get install ca-certificates curl

sudo install \-m 0755 \-d /etc/apt/keyrings

sudo curl \-fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg \-o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc

sudo chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc

echo   "deb \[arch=$(dpkg \--print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc\] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu   $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION\_CODENAME") stable" |   sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list \> /dev/null

sudo apt-get update

sudo apt-get install docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin

#### **2.4.2 Setup Cloudflare Tunnels** {#2.4.2-setup-cloudflare-tunnels}

Deploy the \`cloudflared\` daemon to expose your services securely without port forwarding on your router:

1\. Go to Cloudflare Zero Trust Dashboard \-\> Networks \-\> Tunnels.

2\. Create a new tunnel (e.g., \`inblue-prod\`).

3\. Run the provided installation command on your server:

   sudo cloudflared service install \<YOUR\_TUNNEL\_TOKEN\>

4\. Map public domains to stable internal service addresses or host ports. Avoid hard-coding dynamic container IP addresses.

#### **2.4.3 Containerization with Dockge (docker-compose.yml)** {#2.4.3-containerization-with-dockge-(docker-compose.yml)}

Use the following \`docker-compose.yml\` excerpt to run the PostgreSQL and Redis infrastructure. Backend, frontend, AI, compiler, and tunnel containers should be added separately for a complete production stack.

version: '3.8'

services:

  postgres\_db:

    image: postgres:16

    container\_name: inblue\_postgres

    environment:

      POSTGRES\_USER: postgres

      POSTGRES\_PASSWORD: your\_password

      POSTGRES\_DB: inblue\_db

    ports:

      \- "5432:5432"

    volumes:

      \- inblue\_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

    restart: unless-stopped

  redis\_cache:

    image: redis:alpine

    container\_name: inblue\_redis

    ports:

      \- "6379:6379"

    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:

  inblue\_pgdata:

\*Note: This is an infrastructure excerpt only. The compiler service also requires access to the Docker daemon to create isolated execution containers.\*

### **2.5 Troubleshooting & Common Errors** {#2.5-troubleshooting-&-common-errors}

When setting up the project locally or in production, developers might encounter the following common issues:

#### **2.5.1 Port 8080 or 5173 Already in Use** {#2.5.1-port-8080-or-5173-already-in-use}

**Symptom:** The Spring Boot or Vite server fails to start, displaying a \`Web server failed to start. Port 8080 was already in use.\` error.

**Solution:**

• Identify the process blocking the port:

  \# Windows

  netstat \-ano | findstr :8080

  taskkill /PID \<PID\> /F


  \# Linux/Mac

  lsof \-i :8080

  kill \-9 \<PID\>

• Alternatively, change the \`server.port\` in \`application.properties\` to \`8081\`.

#### **2.5.2 Database Connection Refused** {#2.5.2-database-connection-refused}

**Symptom:** The backend logs show \`org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: Connection refused\`.

**Solution:**

• Verify that PostgreSQL is running.

• Ensure the \`spring.datasource.password\` matches your actual database password.

• Check if port \`5432\` is correctly exposed if running via Docker.

#### **2.5.3 AI Service Configuration Issues** {#2.5.3-ai-service-configuration-issues}

**Symptom:** When calling the AI endpoints, an error stating \`type "vector" does not exist\` occurs.

**Solution:**

• AI service failures are commonly caused by missing or incorrect service URLs, API keys, or unavailable containers.

• Verify the Gemini API key, AnythingLLM endpoint, Python service URLs, and container status. No additional database extension is required.

#### **2.5.4 Invalid PayOS Checksum** {#2.5.4-invalid-payos-checksum}

**Symptom:** When completing a transaction, the system throws a \`Signature validation failed\` exception.

**Solution:**

• Verify that the \`PAYOS\_CHECKSUM\_KEY\` in your \`.env\` perfectly matches the Checksum Key provided in the PayOS Merchant Dashboard. Any discrepancy will cause webhook validation to fail.

#### **2.5.5 Redis Session Timeout** {#2.5.5-redis-session-timeout}

**Symptom:** Users are frequently logged out, or AI chat states are lost during the Pause/Resume feature.

**Solution:**

• Check the Redis container status: \`docker ps | grep redis\`.

• Ensure \`spring.data.redis.host\` is correctly pointing to the Redis instance.

## **3\. User Manual\[\[\*CHỈNH SỬA\*\]\]**  {#3.-user-manual[[*chỉnh-sửa*]]}

### **3.1 Overview** {#3.1-overview}

INBLUE is an AI-powered recruitment simulation platform for Candidates, Mentors, Staff, and Administrators. Candidates use the Web Portal to manage their profiles, apply for job descriptions, complete assessment rounds, schedule interviews, and track application progress. Mentors manage interview sessions and submit candidate evaluations. Staff perform application grading and HR assessments. Administrators manage users, companies, job descriptions, interview pipelines, and assessment content. The Java Spring Boot backend manages authentication, candidate profiles, job descriptions, applications, assessment rounds, payments, notifications, mentor sessions, kiosk bookings, and submissions. The platform integrates AnythingLLM for CV analysis, email evaluation, and code review evaluation. The Python LLM service supports CV and job-description parsing, AI interview orchestration, speech synthesis, and live transcription. Coding submissions are executed in an isolated Docker sandbox with network restrictions and resource limits. The platform supports both web-based and physical kiosk-based AI Interview flows. In the kiosk flow, candidates book a physical kiosk slot through the Web Portal and use a six-digit PIN to start the interview on the kiosk application.

### **3.2 Workflow 1: Manage Candidate Profile and CV** {#3.2-workflow-1:-manage-candidate-profile-and-cv}

**Purpose:** Help Candidates build, update, and upload their CV for automated profile extraction.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** Sign in as a Candidate on the Web Portal and open the Candidate Dashboard.

2. **Step 2:** Navigate to the Profile or Account Settings section.

3. **Step 3:** Review existing profile details, including contact information, education, experience, technical skills, soft skills, and uploaded documents.

4. **Step 4:** Select “Upload CV”, choose a PDF document from the local machine, and confirm the upload.

5. **Step 5:** The backend sends the CV to the AnythingLLM CV parsing workspace and extracts structured profile data such as skills, education, work experience, projects, certifications, and achievements.

6. **Step 6:** Inspect the extracted details, manually correct any discrepancies in the form fields, and click “Save Profile”.

### **3.3 Workflow 2: Search Jobs, Purchase, and Apply** {#3.3-workflow-2:-search-jobs,-purchase,-and-apply}

**Purpose:** Guide Candidates through searching job descriptions, completing payment when required, and submitting applications.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** Open the Job Search tab on the Candidate Dashboard to browse available job descriptions.

2. **Step 2:** Select a Job Card to inspect the company, position, requirements, salary information, price, and assessment pipeline.

3. **Step 3:** If the position is free, click “Apply Now”. If it requires payment, select the purchase or application package option.

4. **Step 4:** For paid job descriptions, complete the PayOS checkout flow. After a successful payment webhook, the backend creates a JdPurchase record with the PURCHASED status.

5. **Step 5:** Confirm the application to link the Candidate Profile and initialize the application workspace.

6. **Step 6:** Open Application History or the Application Workspace to view the active assessment rounds.

### **3.4 Workflow 3: CV Screening** {#3.4-workflow-3:-cv-screening}

**Purpose:** Guide Candidates through submitting their CV for automated comparison with the job requirements.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** In the Application Workspace, select the CV Screening round.

2. **Step 2:** Upload the Candidate CV or use the CV already attached to the application.

3. **Step 3:** Click “Analyze CV” to submit the CV.

4. **Step 4:** The AI evaluation compares the CV with the job requirements and returns Overall CV Match, Skills Match Score, CV Readability Score, Education Match Score, Experience Match Score, Keyword Density, Strengths, Weaknesses, and Potential Red Flags.

5. **Step 5:** Review the AI score and feedback. The application proceeds according to the configured pass threshold and round progression rules.

### **3.5 Workflow 4: Email Simulator** {#3.5-workflow-4:-email-simulator}

**Purpose:** Evaluate the Candidate’s ability to communicate professionally in a recruitment-related email scenario.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** Select the Email Simulator round in the Application Workspace.

2. **Step 2:** Read the scenario describing the recruiter request or project situation.

3. **Step 3:** Review the recruiter email address, required subject code, and suggested email content.

4. **Step 4:** Open the Gmail compose window from the application.

5. **Step 5:** Write the email with an appropriate subject, greeting, response content, and sign-off.

6. **Step 6:** Include the required subject code in the email subject using the format \[INBLUE-APP-applicationId\].

7. **Step 7:** Send the email from Gmail.

8. **Step 8:** The backend scheduler scans the mailbox and identifies the submitted email.

9. **Step 9:** The system stores the email submission and sends it for evaluation.

10. **Step 10:** Return to the Application Workspace to view the processing status and evaluation result.

### **3.6 Workflow 5: Quiz** {#3.6-workflow-5:-quiz}

**Purpose:** Guide Candidates through completing a timed multiple-choice assessment.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** Open the Quiz round and click “Start Quiz”.

2. **Step 2:** Review the time limit, number of questions, passing score, and exam instructions.

3. **Step 3:** Select answers for the questions.

4. **Step 4:** Use “Next” and “Previous” to navigate between questions.

5. **Step 5:** Use the flag action to mark questions for later review.

6. **Step 6:** Review any code snippets included in the question content.

7. **Step 7:** Monitor the countdown timer during the examination.

8. **Step 8:** Click “Submit Quiz” and confirm the submission.

9. **Step 9:** If the timer reaches zero, the system automatically submits the quiz.

10. **Step 10:** The backend grades the answers, calculates the percentage score, compares it with the configured pass threshold, and completes the round.

11. **Step 11:** If the Candidate passes, the application proceeds to the next configured round.

### **3.7 Workflow 6: Coding** {#3.7-workflow-6:-coding}

**Purpose:** Evaluate Candidate hands-on algorithm design and programming skills using an embedded Monaco IDE.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** Open the Coding round and enter the Code Workspace.

2. **Step 2:** Review the problem statement, constraints, time limit, memory limit, and sample test cases.

3. **Step 3:** Select a language supported by the configured compiler sandbox, such as Java, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C\#, Go, Kotlin, Swift, Ruby, PHP, Dart, Scala, or Racket.

4. **Step 4:** Write or edit the solution in the code editor.

5. **Step 5:** Click “Run Code” to execute the solution against visible sample test cases.

6. **Step 6:** Review the compilation or runtime status, passed test cases, execution time, and error output.

7. **Step 7:** Click “Submit” when the solution is ready.

8. **Step 8:** The backend executes the submitted solution in the Docker sandbox against the configured test cases.

9. **Step 9:** Review the final score and test results returned by the assessment service.

### **3.8 Workflow 7: Code Review** {#3.8-workflow-7:-code-review}

**Purpose:** Guide Candidates through reviewing an existing codebase and submitting findings and recommendations.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** Open the Code Review round in the Application Workspace.

2. **Step 2:** Read the review requirements, problem statement, source files, and expected issues.

3. **Step 3:** Inspect the provided code files.

4. **Step 4:** Add review findings, comments, and recommendations for the selected files.

5. **Step 5:** Submit the code review.

6. **Step 6:** The backend sends the submission to AnythingLLM using the CODE\_REVIEW workspace.

### **3.9 Workflow 8: AI Interview Using a Physical Kiosk** {#3.9-workflow-8:-ai-interview-using-a-physical-kiosk}

**Purpose:** Guide Candidates through completing an AI Interview using a scheduled physical kiosk session.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** Open the AI Interview round in the Application Workspace.

2. **Step 2:** View active kiosks, their locations, and available schedules.

3. **Step 3:** Select a kiosk and an available time slot.

4. **Step 4:** Confirm the booking.

5. **Step 5:** The backend creates the booking and generates a six-digit PIN.

6. **Step 6:** The PIN is displayed in the application and included in an in-app notification.

7. **Step 7:** Arrive at the selected kiosk during the scheduled time.

8. **Step 8:** Enter the PIN on the kiosk application.

9. **Step 9:** The backend validates the PIN, kiosk, booking, and allowed entry window. Entry is allowed within approximately fifteen minutes before or after the scheduled start time.

10. **Step 10:** The kiosk starts the AI Interview session.

11. **Step 11:** Answer the interview questions using the kiosk microphone and display.

12. **Step 12:** After the session is completed, the system stores the interview history, AI score, AI evaluation result, and feedback.

13. **Step 13:** View the interview result in the Application Workspace.

### **3.10 Workflow 9: Mentor Interview** {#3.10-workflow-9:-mentor-interview}

**Purpose:** Guide Candidates through mentor assignment, interview scheduling, mentor evaluation, and feedback collection.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** Admin or Staff opens the Mentor Review Assignment area.

2. **Step 2:** Review applications with the AWAITING\_MENTOR status.

3. **Step 3:** Assign one mentor directly, or assign multiple mentors for the Candidate to choose from.

4. **Step 4:** If multiple mentors are assigned, the Candidate selects a mentor from the available list.

5. **Step 5:** The Candidate selects the interview date, start time, duration, and session mode.

6. **Step 6:** For Online mode, the system creates a Daily.co video room and provides a room link.

7. **Step 7:** For Offline mode, the system stores the in-person meeting information.

8. **Step 8:** At the scheduled time, the Candidate joins the online room or attends the agreed physical location.

9. **Step 9:** The Mentor submits a rating, STAR-based notes, strengths, weaknesses, and comments.

10. **Step 10:** After the session, the Candidate may submit a separate mentor rating and comment.

11. **Step 11:** When the required review and feedback records are available, the backend calculates the final score and compares it with the configured pass threshold.

12. **Step 12:** The system marks the round as passed or failed and changes the round status to COMPLETED.

13. **Step 13:** The application proceeds to the next configured round, and the Candidate can view the outcome and available feedback.

7. **Step 7:** The system stores the AI score, AI feedback, detected issues, strengths, weaknesses, and configured metrics with the AI\_EVALUATED status.

8. **Step 8:** Staff opens the application grading area to review the Candidate submission and AI evaluation.

9. **Step 9:** Staff enters the HR score and notes, then marks the round as Pass or Fail.

10. **Step 10:** The round changes to COMPLETED and the application advances only after the staff grading action.

### **3.11 Workflow 10: Configure Job Pipeline and Assessment Content** {#3.11-workflow-10:-configure-job-pipeline-and-assessment-content}

**Purpose:** Guide Administrators through configuring companies, job descriptions, interview pipelines, and assessment content.

**Detailed Guide:**

1. **Step 1:** Sign in as an Administrator and open Admin Dashboard → Company Management.

2. **Step 2:** Create or update a company and upload or update its logo when required.

3. **Step 3:** Create a Job Description and associate it with the selected company.

4. **Step 4:** Open the interview process or template configuration.

5. **Step 5:** Add and order the required assessment rounds.

6. **Step 6:** Configure each round’s name, type, order, maximum score, pass threshold, time limit, and round-specific settings.

7. **Step 7:** Configure quiz questions for Quiz rounds.

8. **Step 8:** Select or manage coding problems for Coding rounds.

9. **Step 9:** Select or manage code review problems for Code Review rounds.

10. **Step 10:** Configure the required settings for Mentor Review and AI Interview rounds.

11. **Step 11:** Save the interview process template.

12. **Step 12:** Save or activate the Job Description after verifying the company, requirements, price, and assessment pipeline.
